prompt:
High-fidelity desktop web UI design comp, landscape, for the organizer dashboard of a retreat-planning survey product. This is a designed interface screen, not a poster: it must read as a screenshot of a working admin product.

Layout scaffold, top to bottom, single column page on a solid warm near-black background (#0b0908, no photograph): Masthead row: far left a small uppercase tracked label "THE ATMOSPHERIC BUILDERS' RETREAT", beneath it a large ultra-condensed tall white grotesque headline "ORGANIZER." in capitals; far right a fully rounded white pill button with black text "Export CSV" and beside it a quieter text line "Closes Aug 15". Below the masthead: one full-width horizontal ledger strip of six stat pairs separated by thin 1px white hairline rules above and below — "RESPONSES 37", "YES 24", "MAYBE 9", "NO 4", "NEED TRAVEL HELP 11", "DAYS LEFT 8" — small tracked uppercase labels with larger white numerals. Center band, the dominant region (about 40% of the viewport): a calendar availability heatmap titled with a small condensed header "WHEN CAN THEY COME"; three month grids side by side labeled SEPTEMBER, OCTOBER, NOVEMBER; each day is a small rounded square filled white at an opacity proportional to availability — bright white means many people available, very faint means few, with faint small day numbers inside; a few edge cells are split horizontally, top half bright and bottom half faint. Under the heatmap: a short ledger titled "BEST WINDOWS" of three hairline rows like "THU OCT 8 – SUN OCT 11 · 29 OF 33 AVAILABLE" with the first row brightest. Bottom region, two columns: left two-thirds a responses table with thin hairline-separated rows, each row showing a small circular avatar, a handle like @maren.dev, a name, city, an interest word (YES/MAYBE/NO), travel answer, and a count of date ranges; right one-third a narrow column with a "LOCATIONS" ranked tally ledger (Palm Springs, Joshua Tree, San Diego, Coachella Valley, LA metro with small tally numerals) above an "ALLOWLIST" panel of small white outlined handle chips and an "add handles" underline input. Page bottom is cut off mid-table implying scroll.

Every interface element is pure white at varying opacity on the near-black ground; no second UI color, no cards, no boxes, no shadows; thin 1px hairline rules structure everything; subtle film grain overall; flat matte finish, no gloss, no 3D. No browser chrome.
